public_body: Barnstable Town Council Subcommittee To Review Zoning And Permitting Regulations
overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. No separate steering committee existed, the May 2 notice was timely posted to the Town's official notice page, and minutes need only be available on request, not posted online. The 2017 assertions were declined as outside the complaint.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the subcommittee held meetings of a claimed 'steering committee' on short-term rentals without posting any notice.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that a separate steering committee existed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the May 2 meeting notice was improperly posted only under the Town homepage link, not on the subcommittee's own webpage.
allegations.key_passage: we find that where the notice was timely posted to the page on the Town’s website where all meeting notices are posted, the Subcommittee satisfied the posting requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the subcommittee failed to post minutes of its July 2018 to February 2019 meetings to its webpage.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Subcommittee did not violate the Open Meeting Law by failing to post its meeting minutes to a website.

allegations.summary: Request for further review raised new assertions about the validity of the 2017 creation of the ad hoc zoning subcommittee, outside the original complaint.
allegations.key_passage: Our office does not conduct broad audits of public bodies and will seek to address only allegations made in the Open Meeting Law complaint in order to give a public body a chance to address those allegations.
